A1.justification: The authors, DLA/MESSy pipeline, and matching original results establish the same research work despite retitling. All supplied pages are readable, but both PDFs end with references and omit the supplementary material cited for generation details, layer ablations, and clustering checks. Those referenced materials cannot be compared.

before.justification: Section 4 reports original teacher and student classification experiments, modality ablations, latent-alignment measurements, class-level analyses, and generation-efficiency measurements.

after.justification: V2 retains those original experiments and adds controlled comparisons, CIFAR-100 transfer results, and ImageNet-1K evaluation.

M1.justification: Both versions use undecoded audio/3D latents, Perceiver-based teacher fusion, and multilayer prediction of pooled auxiliary-modality features from student classification tokens. V2 specifies predictor architecture, filtering, and loss weights more fully, without establishing a change to the proposed procedure.

E1.justification: V2 retains Imagenette2-320, Caltech101, and ImageNet-100, while adding full ImageNet-1K classification and CIFAR-100 linear-probe transfer from ImageNet-100-trained students. These substantially expand class coverage and introduce evaluation on a different downstream population.

E2.justification: V2 adds the architecture-matched Raw+Perc teacher comparison in Table 1 and the CLS-Pred student comparator in Table 4. Figure 6 also adds LUGPI to the alignment comparison previously containing only the image baseline and MESSy. These substantially strengthen comparisons around the method's central mechanisms; the original KD/LUGPI accuracy comparisons remain.

E3.justification: New evaluation designs include freezing ImageNet-100 students for CIFAR-100 linear probing, matching raw and latent teachers' Perceiver resamplers, and controlling prediction targets and teacher representations in Table 4. Existing ViT-B/16, token budgets, dropout, and clustering counts remain; newly disclosed training hyperparameters do not establish changes to existing experiments.

E4.justification: V2 tests whether gains arise from resampler architecture, predictor heads versus auxiliary-modality targets, and latent versus raw teachers. It also adds transfer evidence concerning visual discriminability, LUGPI alignment analysis, and four additional class cases. These extend the original modality ablations and synesthesia analyses substantially.

E5.justification: Both versions state three independent runs. V2 explicitly identifies table entries as means with standard deviations and plots as means, clarifying v1's unspecified ± notation. However, the new ImageNet-1K and approximate raw-teacher results omit uncertainty despite that general statement; no increased run count is established.

E6.justification: Original accuracy entries and baseline/MESSy alignment values are retained. Added outcomes include CLS-Pred's 67.04% on ImageNet-100, CIFAR-100 probe accuracies of 42.4% for LUGPI and 48.1% for MESSy, and ImageNet-1K accuracies of 64.17%, 71.32%, and 69.05% for image-only, teacher, and MESSy respectively. Raw+Perc, raw-teacher students, LUGPI alignment, and additional class results further expand the evidence.

T1.justification: V2 retains the original data-processing inequality and adds a chain-rule derivation showing that joint modalities cannot decrease mutual information with the label (Section 3.1, Equations 2–3). This is a limited extension of the mathematical argument, without a new substantial theorem or proof.

C1.justification: The central claims remain that DLA bypasses the decode-encode loop, MESSy transfers auxiliary priors without harmful rigid feature matching, and image-only students exhibit synesthetic alignment without extra inference overhead. The new contribution list and title reorganize claims already present in v1.

C2.justification: V2 adds interpretations attributing gains primarily to latent representations rather than resampling, and to auxiliary prediction targets rather than predictor architecture alone. It newly argues that handcrafted-feature alignment excludes label co-occurrence and interprets transfer results as evidence against capacity interference. The conclusion also identifies frozen generators as limiting task-specific latent co-adaptation.

D1.justification: V2 newly specifies generator variants, four acoustic codebooks, eight-head resamplers, two-layer prediction heads, caption regeneration using class-name synonyms, and the weighted training objective. Section 4.1 adds 50-epoch teacher/student budgets, student training from scratch, AdamW, cosine scheduling, temperature 2.0, and loss weights. These substantially improve documentation without demonstrating that existing settings changed.

R1.justification: The short prior-work discussion becomes three substantive subsections. V2 discusses BYOL, data2vec, AV-data2vec, JEPA, CRD, and projector-based cross-modal distillation, explicitly identifying AV-data2vec as the closest architectural predecessor. It positions MESSy around synthetic auxiliary-modality targets while acknowledging that predictive heads follow established designs.

P1.justification: V2 substantially rewrites and expands the introduction, related work, method exposition, and experimental narrative. It introduces an explicit contribution list, separates the method into motivation and three stages, and gives setup and scalability their own subsections. This is extensive narrative restructuring beyond the added experiments.

P2.justification: The document changes from two-column to single-column layout. V2 adds Figures 3–5 redisplaying existing table results, redraws alignment as three dataset panels with LUGPI, expands the class chart from six to ten examples, restructures Tables 1–2, and adds ablation and scalability tables. The original conceptual and pipeline diagrams are retained.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially addresses v1's attribution gaps through Raw+Perc and CLS-Pred controls, while transfer and ImageNet-1K experiments broaden validation. Fuller implementation details and explicit acknowledgment of architectural predecessors also improve assessability. Supplementary material remains unavailable, some new results lack uncertainty, and several causal and information-theoretic interpretations overstate the evidence, but these limitations do not outweigh the substantial gains in experimental support and transparency.
